terms.gloss: At my expense: it’s on me.
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 328–329: Nempe dē tuō? — Dē meō.
Ter. Ad. 117: scortātur, pōtat, olet unguenta? dē meō
terms.comment: Dē meō, “out of my own purse”, stands alone as an answer in Plautus and Terence; dē suō is the same of another person. The plain sentence Ego solvam says it too.

terms.gloss: scot-free: paying nothing towards a meal
evidence: Ter. Ph. 339: tēn asymbolum venīre ūnctum atque lautum ē balineīs
terms.comment: The guest whose dinner someone else pays for (Lewis & Short: “that contributes nothing to an entertainment, scot-free”).

phrases.english: It’s on me; don’t get your purse out.

phrases.latin: bene volō ego illī facere, sī tū nōn nevīs. — Nempe dē tuō? — Dē meō: nam quod tuomst meumst, omne meumst autem tuom.
phrases.english: I want to do him a kindness, if you don’t object. — Out of your own pocket, I take it? — Out of mine: for what is yours is mine, and all that is mine is yours.

phrases.latin: scortātur, pōtat, olet unguenta? dē meō
phrases.english: He goes with girls, he drinks, he smells of scent? It’s at my expense.

sources: Lewis & Short: meus · Lewis & Short: asymbolus
